decisions.quote: We propose a benchmark to measure whether a language model is truthful in generating answers to questions.

decisions.problem: What evidence to collect (e.g., direct model answers vs probes)
decisions.did: The evidence collected involves model responses to the TruthfulQA questions to assess truthfulness; mentions testing GPT-3, GPT-Neo/J, GPT-2 and a T5-based model.
decisions.stated_reason: The benchmark measures truthfulness of generated answers rather than other properties.
decisions.quote: The benchmark comprises 817 questions that span 38 categories, including health, law, finance and politics.

decisions.problem: Whether to accept a result
decisions.did: The paper reports that the best model was truthful on 58% of questions while human performance was 94%, and notes that larger models tended to be less truthful.
decisions.stated_reason: Report observed performance and contrast with human performance to assess result acceptance.
decisions.quote: The best model was truthful on 58% of questions, while human performance was 94%.

decisions.problem: Whether to continue or drop a line of work
decisions.did: The authors discuss that scaling up models alone is less promising for improving truthfulness and suggest fine-tuning with training objectives other than imitation of text from the web.
decisions.stated_reason: This contrasts with other NLP tasks and motivates exploring different objectives for truthfulness.
decisions.quote: However, this result is expected if false answers are learned from the training distribution.

decisions.problem: How to interpret an ambiguous result
decisions.did: They acknowledge that false answers can arise from imitative falsehoods vs non-imitative weaknesses (syntax/style), and distinguish core weaknesses.
decisions.stated_reason: They define a “weakness” and distinguish imitative vs non-imitative falsehoods to interpret errors.
decisions.quote: If a model returns a false answer to a question in our benchmark, this could be because the answer is an imitative falsehood. However, it could also be caused by the syntax or style of the question.

decisions.problem: How strongly to state a claim
decisions.did: The authors discuss broader implications, suggesting scalability alone is not enough and that future work could test more diverse or larger models
decisions.stated_reason: To temper conclusions about scaling and truthfulness, acknowledging possible limitations and future directions.
decisions.quote: Future work could test whether more diverse or larger models produce the same kind of falsehoods on TruthfulQA.
